northeast curb, about 66 feet northwest of the intersection with [roadway], where a crosswalk was located. witness 1, who's information is on related [case id], stated she was directly behind unit 1, [roadway], when she observed the pedestrian walking northbound [roadway] area. witness 1 stated [roadway], to avoid the pedestrian, when unit 1 struck the pedestrian. witness stated that she and driver 1 were going a speed above the posted speed limit. driver 1 stated [roadway], [roadway], not going anywhere specific, when all of a sudden there was a loud thud sound. driver 1 stated she swerved than braked and came to a stop. driver 1 stated she never saw the pedestrian, until after the thud sound. driver 1 stated she was going about 30 mph when the collision occurred. driver 1 was approaching an area that was on a slight uphill grade, [roadway] was making a slight turn to the right, [roadway] design and striping. this area was also at the end of a construction zone, and near an intersection, that has a high volume of pedestrian traffic. with all of these roadway hazards existing, driver 1 failed to reduce her speed appropriately, [roadway] at an unsafe speed. unit 2 the pedestrian, failed to yield right of way to the traffic on the roadway, [roadway] other than a crosswalk, that was 60 feet southeast of the collision site. unit 1 collided front concentrated, (front right), into the right side of the pedestrian. the pedestrian rolled up onto the hood of the car, and into the windshield and ""a"" pillar, traveling with unit 1, before rolling off the right side of the vehicle in a fender vault, and colliding into the northeast curb. driver 1 reacted and swerved to the left as she was braking and came to a [roadway], about 80 feet northwest of the area of impact, (aoi). the pedestrian traveled about 55 feet from aoi to final rest. dallas fire / rescue 24 transported the pedestrian to [medical facility] in dallas, [roadway]. lovitt pronounced the pedestrian deceased on [date] at 1842, from severe blunt force trauma to the skull. using crash math formulas for time and distance, along with the searle throw formula, i/o determined that the speed of unit 1 was traveling about 33 mph, which is unsafe for the area. this is dallas police traffic fatality 132 for 2018. this report is incomplete pending toxicology results from the dallas county medical examiners office. *** on [date] this report was supplemented to add factor 67, under the influence of alcohol and factor 68, under the influence of drugs, to unit 2, the pedestrian. the +/-13. 9 ng/ml, benzoylecgonine: 410. 1 +/-65. 6 ng/ml. this report is now complete. ***

the listed address in regards to a traffic collision involving a pedestrian. the officer arrived and met with the below individuals. wi-01: juan estrella jr.//[date]// 4947 sun valley el paso tx. 79924. the witness said he was w on edgemere at a stop when he saw the pedestrian begin to cross edgemere on the eastern cross walk of the intersection from s to n. the witness saw u1 turning from geronimo (facing n) onto edgemere by making a right turn on a green light but also facing the pedestrian walk sign. the witness stated he saw the pedestrian being struck from behind and fall onto the hood of u1 and then to the ground. the witness exited his vehicle stopped traffic and tended to the pedestrian and noticed the large cut on the back of the pedestrian's head as a result of the accident. wi-02: myra ley // [date] // 3448 billet hill el paso tx 79936. the witness told the investigator that she was traveling n on geronimo and saw the pedestrian n on the eastern cross walk of geronimo and edgemere and u1 making a right turn from geronimo onto edgemere. the witness stated she felt that u1 was not going to stop and then she saw u1 strike the pedestrian at which time she exited her vehicle and assisted the pedestrian. driver of u1 said he was n on geronimo and was making a r turn to head e on edgemere. the driver said he saw the green light for n traffic on geronimo but did not see the pedestrian already crossing on the cross walk until he had struck him. the driver stated he told the pedestrian he was sorry and that he did not mean to ""run him over"" but there was a language barrier and he felt the witnesses were getting aggressive toward him so he remained in his vehicle [medical facility] where he stated he was crossing edgemere s to n when suddenly he was hit. the pedestrian stated he did not know what kind of vehicle hit him all he felt was the impact and then falling. the pedestrian complained of pain to the back of his head due to the cut [medical facility] for medical evaluation. the driver of u1 commented that he did not see the pedestrian due to a brush of some sort inside the gas station property at the corner of the intersection but the vegetation did not obstruct the view of the cross walk at all. the driver of u1 was cited for the accident.

records.deidentified_narrative: on november 23rd, 2018 at approximately 2059 hours, i, officer a armstrong with the justin police department was dispatched to an accident at 700 fm 156 s involving a pedestrian. the caller advised that he believed the pedestrian was deceased [roadway]. when i arrived on scene, i observed a bystander performing cpr on the male pedestrian (unit 2). i also observed debris in the roadway from the vehicle that hit unit 2, however, the vehicle was not at the location. i advised my dispatch that this was a hit and run accident. i spoke with a female witness on scene who stated that unit 2 was her husband. she stated that the vehicle was black and traveling southbound on fm 156. i requested several units to the area to be on the lookout of the actor vehicle. i advised all units that the vehicle would have extensive damage and would be missing the passenger side mirror. next, i took over for the bystander and administered cpr for several minutes until justin fire department medics arrived on scene. after medics arrived, i spoke with the victims wife. she advised that her and unit 2 were walking southbound on fm 156. she stated that unit 2 was walking partially on the roadway in the southbound lanes while she was walking next to him in the construction area. she stated that out of nowhere, a black in color vehicle traveling at a high rate of speed struck unit 2 throwing him high into the air and causing him to flip several times. she stated that unit 2 [roadway] of traffic on his back. she said that he sat up and was struggling to breath. she stated that he rolled over [roadway] in the construction area, then lost consciousness. she then said that she flagged a passerby down for help which is when 9-1-1 was dialed. medics then transported unit 2 to medical city denton where he was pronounced deceased at 2155 hours. while processing the scene, i was advised by dispatch that the driver of the actor vehicle (unit 1) call 9-1-1 to report that she believed she struck something at that location on 156. i went to the actors current location with several units to interview her. upon arrival, i observed unit 1. unit 1 had significant damage to the windshield on the passenger side. i also observed moderate damage to the right headlight and front passenger side bumper. i spoke with the driver of unit 1 who stated that she and her passenger stopped as soon as possible after the collision. she stated that they both exited the vehicle and looked behind them. she said they did not see anything so she thought it was an animal. the driver then advised that they continued driving to their destination. she said that upon arrival, they decided to go back to the scene to look for anything that might have been hit. the driver said that as she approached the scene, she observed several emergency vehicles. she said at that point in time, she knew something was wrong. the driver said that she attempted to speak with an officer directing traffic at the scene but was told to turn around due to the roadway being closed. the driver said she then drove back to the residence and dialed 9-1-1 to report what had happened. neither the driver nor passenger were able to give a definitive point of collision on the roadway. next, i traveled to medical city denton for a voluntary blood draw for the driver. after the blood draw, i made contact with the victims wife. she advised that she did not know exactly where the incident occurred, but she did now that it was just a little bit after the bridge. based on the interviews and the lack of skid marks on the roadway, the exact point of impact was unable to be determined. a report will be filed with the district attorneys office and a grand jury will determine if the driver of the vehicle will face charges. on march 28th, 2019 i attended a grand jury hearing regarding this accident. i was later notified that the no billed and will not face charges. i also received the toxicology from the texas department of public safety which showed that there were no drugs or alcohol in the driver's system.

records.public_safe_text: on november 23rd, 2018 at approximately 2059 hours, i, officer a armstrong with the justin police department was dispatched to an accident at 700 fm 156 s involving a pedestrian. the caller advised that he believed the pedestrian was deceased [roadway]. when i arrived on scene, i observed a bystander performing cpr on the male pedestrian (unit 2). i also observed debris in the roadway from the vehicle that hit unit 2, however, the vehicle was not at the location. i advised my dispatch that this was a hit and run accident. i spoke with a female witness on scene who stated that unit 2 was her husband. she stated that the vehicle was black and traveling southbound on fm 156. i requested several units to the area to be on the lookout of the actor vehicle. i advised all units that the vehicle would have extensive damage and would be missing the passenger side mirror. next, i took over for the bystander and administered cpr for several minutes until justin fire department medics arrived on scene. after medics arrived, i spoke with the victims wife. she advised that her and unit 2 were walking southbound on fm 156. she stated that unit 2 was walking partially on the roadway in the southbound lanes while she was walking next to him in the construction area. she stated that out of nowhere, a black in color vehicle traveling at a high rate of speed struck unit 2 throwing him high into the air and causing him to flip several times. she stated that unit 2 [roadway] of traffic on his back. she said that he sat up and was struggling to breath. she stated that he rolled over [roadway] in the construction area, then lost consciousness. she then said that she flagged a passerby down for help which is when 9-1-1 was dialed. medics then transported unit 2 to medical city denton where he was pronounced deceased at 2155 hours. while processing the scene, i was advised by dispatch that the driver of the actor vehicle (unit 1) call 9-1-1 to report that she believed she struck something at that location on 156. i went to the actors current location with several units to interview her. upon arrival, i observed unit 1. unit 1 had significant damage to the windshield on the passenger side. i also observed moderate damage to the right headlight and front passenger side bumper. i spoke with the driver of unit 1 who stated that she and her passenger stopped as soon as possible after the collision. she stated that they both exited the vehicle and looked behind them. she said they did not see anything so she thought it was an animal. the driver then advised that they continued driving to their destination. she said that upon arrival, they decided to go back to the scene to look for anything that might have been hit. the driver said that as she approached the scene, she observed several emergency vehicles. she said at that point in time, she knew something was wrong. the driver said that she attempted to speak with an officer directing traffic at the scene but was told to turn around due to the roadway being closed. the driver said she then drove back to the residence and dialed 9-1-1 to report what had happened. neither the driver nor passenger were able to give a definitive point of collision on the roadway. next, i traveled to medical city denton for a voluntary blood draw for the driver. after the blood draw, i made contact with the victims wife. she advised that she did not know exactly where the incident occurred, but she did now that it was just a little bit after the bridge. based on the interviews and the lack of skid marks on the roadway, the exact point of impact was unable to be determined. a report will be filed with the district attorneys office and a grand jury will determine if the driver of the vehicle will face charges. on march 28th, 2019 i attended a grand jury hearing regarding this accident. i was later notified that the no billed and will not face charges. i also received the toxicology from the texas department of public safety which showed that there were no drugs or alcohol in the driver's system.

records.public_safe_text: on [date], i, officer b. tyner #336, was dispatched to 7205 [roadway] (plano sports academy mckinney) for a motor vehicle accident involving a pedestrian. after receiving the call, i drove code 3 (lights and sirens) in my mckinney issued police patrol vehicle to the location. upon my arrival, i located (unit 2) tracy stout (w/f [date]) in the parking lot of plano sports academy mckinney. tracy advised while walking in the parking lot with shemeeka burnett-davison (b/f [date]), she noticed a (unit 1) black cadillac escalade (texas tag#[identifier]) traveling towards her direction. tracy advised she was near the middle of the roadway, attempting to cross over to another section of the parking lot. tracy stated she started to wave at the cadillac, however the front right passenger tire of the cadillac, drove over her right foot/leg. tracy advised after her leg was driven over, she fell down onto the ground, hurting her right arm and wrist in the process. i spoke with shemeeka who advised she was near tracy when she was struck by the cadillac. shemeeka advised tracy was attempting to cross over to another section of the parking lot with the cadillac. shemeeka advised it appeared the cadillac had driven over tracy's right leg with the front passenger side. i also spoke with kelly charland (w/f [date]) who advised she is tracy's sister. kelly stated she witnessed the black cadillac driving over tracy's right leg and tracy falling down onto the ground. i spoke to (unit 1) lacey combs (w/f [date]) who was the driver of the cadillac. lacey stated she was facing westbound and was turning southbound in the parking lot. lacey advised while traveling southbound in the parking lot, she first noticed tracy running in the parking lot. lacey stated while passing tracy, she heard a thud on right side of her car, however she does not believe ran over tracy's leg with the vehicle. when i spoke to lacey again, she advised she did not see tracy, but again stated she does not believe she hit tracy with her vehicle. the mckinney fire department arrived on scene and assisted tracy into the ambulance. while being seen by the fire department, there were no obvious signs that tracy right foot/leg was driven over by the cadillac. it should be noted it was a very wet day, however her tracy's black tights, were not covered in dirt, [roadway]. when examining tracy's leg, there were no visible injuries on her leg tracy advised her right arm and wrist hurt from falling down. i also did not observe any visible injuries to her arm or wrist. she was transported to medical city mckinney for further evaluations. i spoke to a worker at the plano sports academy mckinney who advised video could not be seen at this time. i was advised they would contact their director and would attempt to retrieve video of the incident at a later time. i left the worker with the [case id] for the incidentwitness information:burnett-davison, shemeeka latrice - phone # (214) 404-5823charland, kelly elise - no phone #
